_what: Named run modes. A mode is a stated INTENT — 'resume the writer' — and the set of steps that intent turns off.
_why: On 2026-08-13 an operator asked for a writer resume. It was launched with three environment
variables and needed six, so the CPA pre-pass, the pre-phase skill assessment and the
regression guard all ran anyway — each is a separate default-ACTIVE step, and nothing tied
any of them to the stated intent. The operator had to notice it mid-run.
The intent already existed in run-checkpoint.sh's pre-writer stage, reachable only through a
checkpoint, and even that list omitted the regression guard. Two half-definitions of one idea.
Declared here, the engine reads a mode and never knows one. Adding a mode is an edit to this
file. Nobody assembles a mode by hand, so no mode can be half-applied.

writer-only._what: Resume at the writer. The spec pass, roster mint, Jira ingest, CPA pre-pass, pre-phase skill assessment and regression baseline have all already run, or are not wanted for this attempt.
writer-only._cost: Skipping the regression baseline means later test gates judge the codeline's CURRENT state, so pre-existing failures can be attributed to this change. Right for testing a writer; wrong for a run you intend to merge.
writer-only._why_no_mint: The mint does NOT run. A writer re-run uses the roster that was already minted and reviewed; re-minting proposes against an existing roster and the merge is additive, so it accumulates near-duplicate roles and changes the agents under a story mid-stream.

post-spec._what: The spec pass and the roster are done and on disk; everything from the CPA pre-pass onward still runs.
post-spec._why_mint: Skips the mint because this mode describes a RESUME of a run whose roster is already on disk — pre-run-reset preserves the registries when EPAM_RESUME_RUN is set. A fresh launch has no such protection, which is why writer-only does not skip it.

post-roster._what: The roster is minted and assignments are written; the spec pass still runs.
post-roster._why_mint: Skips the mint because this mode describes a RESUME of a run whose roster is already on disk — pre-run-reset preserves the registries when EPAM_RESUME_RUN is set. A fresh launch has no such protection, which is why writer-only does not skip it.
